name: Piller Group GmbH (Piller Power Systems)
employees: Around 1,000 worldwide, about 650 of them at Osterode and Bilshausen (company statements 2019–2026; NW-IHK, Feb 2026)
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Piller is Europe's largest maker of rotary and diesel-rotary UPS and, through Active Power, of flywheel UPS — a franchise that lost the hyperscale segment to battery-static UPS over the past decade and has re-entered the AI buildout from the generation side instead: its SHIELDX kinetic stabilizer now ships inside every behind-the-meter gas-engine plant its sister company Bergen Engines sells to US AI data centers, more than 3 GW of them signed by June 2026, and the binding constraint is the Osterode and Bilshausen factories, which are being taken from about 100 to about 400 large systems a year by the end of 2027. BACKGROUND. Founded in Hamburg in 1909 by Anton Piller, in Osterode am Harz since 1919, wholly owned by the privately held UK engineering group Langley Holdings plc since December 2004 (Piller's own history page says 2005), with the former NASDAQ-listed flywheel maker Active Power of Austin, Texas acquired for a nominal price plus assumed liabilities in November 2016. Products: UB-V and UNIBLOCK UBT+ rotary UPS (1.0–3.24 MW per module, paralleled to 40–100 MW), UBTD+ diesel rotary UPS (DRUPS), the Isolated Parallel bus, POWERBRIDGE kinetic energy storage to 60 MJ+ per unit, the CleanSource flywheel UPS family, the M+ Series modular static UPS launched in 2024 to re-enter the segment, aircraft ground power and naval frequency converters, and since August 2025 SHIELDX Dynamic Power Stabilization for islanded AI campuses. Per the Northeim chamber of commerce (Feb 2026), Piller's 2025 revenue was €332M (+28%) on order intake of €370M (+24%); Langley itself discloses only its Power Solutions division (Bergen Engines, Piller, Marelli Motori) — 2025 revenue €793M, orders on hand €1,952M, 2026 forecast €1,346M — and states Piller set records for revenue, profit and order intake in 2023, 2024 and 2025. There is no analyst consensus: Langley is unlisted and its own forward statements are the only expectations on record.
ecosystemRole: We assess Piller as the one vendor in this corpus whose product answers the UPS-room question with a rotating machine rather than power electronics and a battery — the reference for how rotary, diesel-rotary and flywheel UPS differ from the static units Vertiv, Schneider Electric, Eaton and ABB sell, and for what the isolated-parallel bus buys at tens of megawatts. Basis: company product literature and Uptime Institute's account of NEXTDC's Tier IV IP-bus sites. For the AI campus, its relevance has shifted from the hall to the fence line: SHIELDX is a flywheel-and-synchronous-machine stabilizer sold as one unit per 12 MW Bergen Engines gen-set to hold frequency through GPU load steps on islanded plants, which places it beside — and in competition with — the battery buffers this corpus tracks (ON.energy's medium-voltage BESS at the same Crusoe campuses, Tesla Megapacks at xAI per SemiAnalysis). Crusoe, Nebius and Tesla are covered customers; the static-UPS majors are competitors on the hall side; Caterpillar distributed Active Power flywheels as the Cat UPS from 2000 and is now a rival prime-mover OEM to Bergen; Bloom Energy's fuel cells are reported to have displaced the gas-engine plan at the Vineland site third parties tie to the first 400 MW SHIELDX order.

productsAndServices.name: SHIELDX™ Dynamic Power Stabilization — kinetic stabilizer for islanded AI campuses
productsAndServices.description: Launched 21 August 2025 and, per Langley's 2026 interim, incorporated in every behind-the-meter plant the Power Solutions division sells. Per Piller's product page it 'brings together two complementary battery-free technologies': 'A high-inertia electromechanical stabilizer providing continuous voltage and frequency conditioning' and 'Ultra-fast, bi-directional kinetic power modules that absorb or inject active power in real time', in 'A modular, scalable architecture positioned between generation and the data-centre electrical distribution'. Built on Piller's Dynamic Power Conditioning and Stabilization (DPCS) technology — the UB-V synchronous machine, coupling choke and POWERBRIDGE flywheel lineage. Stated performance: voltage and frequency held to ±1%, sub-millisecond response, a reference ratio of one SHIELDX per 12 MW Bergen–Marelli gen-set 'against 25–30% instantaneous load steps', scalable 'to cover 100% load steps with increased ratios', 'true short-circuit contribution, high fault-clearing capability and zero energy storage degradation', 'engineered to meet TIER IV fault-tolerance standards and up to 99.999% uptime'. Sector page: 'large-scale load stabilization (50 MW to 1 GW+)'. No per-module MW or MJ rating, efficiency, harmonic figure or footprint is published.
highlights: Embedded in more than 3 GW of Bergen Engines behind-the-meter orders signed by June 2026: Crusoe (438 MW contract plus 310 MW LOI, June 2026), Liberty Energy (45 × 11.2 MWe, 500 MW+, May 2026) and E-Finity Distributed Generation (36 × 11.2 MW, 400 MW, November 2025) — every counterparty release names Piller

Langley, February 2026: 'AI load profiles are being found to wreak havoc with battery solutions, whereas Piller flywheel technology handles the erratic profiles caused by AI compute with ease' — the company's stated rationale; SemiAnalysis independently describes Bergen selling engines 'with flywheels from a vendor under the same parent company' that inject or absorb real power for 5–30 seconds
Built-to-stock: 'shipment in under 4-6 weeks' per company; a live 12.5 MW Bergen engine plus SHIELD-X demonstration at Osterode is planned for customer tours in autumn 2026

Positioned by the company against oversized generation ('enables right-sizing rather than oversizing'), against BESS ('Avoids C-rate limits, thermal stress, and degradation cycles') and against static UPS, which 'stabilise the load, not the power source'
productsAndServices.positioning: The rotating-mass answer to GPU load swings on islanded gas-engine plants, competing with battery buffers — ON.energy's medium-voltage 'AI UPS' BESS at the same Crusoe campuses and Tesla Megapacks at xAI (per SemiAnalysis) — rather than with static UPS. Its advantages as stated are real inertia, fault current and no storage degradation; its limit is that a flywheel holds seconds, so the battery keeps the duration role. The only rotary stabilizer of this kind in the corpus; the peer set (Hitec, Rolls-Royce Solutions Liège mtu Kinetic PowerPack, Hitzinger) has announced nothing comparable in the AI-plant market.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct through Piller subsidiaries, and bundled into Langley Power Solutions' behind-the-meter plant sales led by Bergen Engines Americas (ShieldX@piller.com / PowerOn@langleyholdings.com); standard off-the-shelf product 'available to the sector for both our own BTM solution and others'.
targetSegments: AI data centers on behind-the-meter islanded generation (100 MW to multi-GW campuses)
Islanded plants with gas turbines, high-speed gen-sets or hybrid configurations
Grid-tied facilities requiring stabilization; retrofit applications
productsAndServices.roadmap: Plant-level: contract to first shipment under 12 months, power-on in 18 months (company); Bergen B36:45V20 12.5 MW engines sold out until Q2 2028; ~€100M divisional capex through 2028 with Piller 'increasing capacity accordingly'. Product-level: no published datasheet or per-module rating yet; the spelling alternates between SHIELDX™ and SHIELD-X in company texts.

productsAndServices.name: UB-V Series rotary UPS — fifth-generation UNIBLOCK™, 1.0–3.24 MW per module
productsAndServices.description: Electrically coupled rotary UPS launched 14 January 2020 in data-centre and industrial variants. Per company pages and the 2021 industrial brochure: '1100kVA 1.0MW to 3600kVA 3.24MW' per module, 'in both battery and kinetic energy storage versions', 'paralleling up to 100MW / 115MVA', 'Available in low or medium voltage levels'; 'on-line efficiency of up to 98% at 100% load and 97% at 50% load when compared with static UPS which typically operate around 96.3% efficiency at both 50% and 100% loads' (IEC 62040-3); 'Wide input voltage tolerance (up to -50%)' — 'can compensate for voltage dips of up to -50% without recourse to stored energy or diesel generators'; 'Handling of load steps up to 100%'; 'no power capacitors or electric fans', MTBF '5 times' that of static UPS, 'off-line service intervals as little as once every five years' with e-VENTLOG remote monitoring. The 'Power of 10' IPCS module combines 'four 2.5MW UB-V Series modules' with two POWERBRIDGE PB21 each behind a '10MW decoupling choke', holding a 20 kV microgrid to '± 8 %' voltage and '± 1 %' frequency with 'more than ten seconds' of ride-through.
highlights: Company claim: 'up to 3.24MW of UPS in a single module' — 'a real alternative to increasingly sprawling multiple static UPS solutions', sized as a 'single-entity building block' matching 3 MW-class IT strings so 'multi-module paralleling' is eliminated

Within twelve months of launch 'evaluated or commissioned to provide more than 1.3GW' across 22 projects at 1.2–3.4 MW each (company webinar release, 2020); named installs include NEXTDC S3/M3 (IP-bus with mtu engines), Helmholtz-Zentrum Berlin (6,750 kW at 10 kV, Nov 2024) and a US semiconductor fab (five 2,700 kW units with PB60 flywheels at 24 kV, >12 MW, no batteries)
Per the charakter.me employer profile (Apr 2026), 3.2 MW systems are in series production for AI load profiles; Seidel: 'the AI boom brings us to our capacity limits'

The 2020 roadmap targeted '5.0MW single-entity medium voltage solutions planned by 2025' and '10.0MW solutions… by decade's end' with Marelli Motori; the 2023 Power of 10 delivers 10 MW as four 2.5 MW modules under one choke — no first-party confirmation that a 5 MW single machine has shipped
productsAndServices.positioning: The high end of the rotary UPS market — Hitec Power Protection (Air Water), Rolls-Royce Solutions Liège (mtu Kinetic PowerPack, 1,250–3,000 kVA units) and Hitzinger are the named peers by product class; against static UPS the company's pitch is fewer modules per megawatt, no capacitors or fans, fault clearing and harmonic isolation, and a medium-voltage option, conceded against static's finer scaling and multi-vendor batteries (Schneider Electric White Paper 222).
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Piller subsidiaries in eleven countries plus agents and distributors in about 38 more; Piller Unity Service Pack service contracts and e-VENTLOG remote monitoring.
targetSegments: Cloud hyperscale, wholesale colocation and large enterprise data centers
Semiconductor fabs, photomask and pharmaceutical plants
Research (synchrotrons, HPC), broadcasting, airports, healthcare, microgrids
productsAndServices.roadmap: Bilshausen expansion (€20M, announced May 2026) to lift output from about 100 to about 400 large systems a year by end-2027, adding 150 jobs; the 5 MW single-entity MV machine remains a stated target without a shipped reference.

productsAndServices.name: UNIBLOCK™ UBT+ rotary UPS, UBTD+ diesel rotary UPS (DRUPS) and the DeRUPS™ configuration
productsAndServices.description: The core platform since the 1970s. UBT+ per the 2018 brochure: 'Single machine sizes from 500kW up to 2700kW'; 'Paralleling up to 40MW' at medium voltage, while 'At low voltages, simple paralleling is limited to about 5MW but there are configurations using fault isolated parallel techniques that allow this to be increased to up to 20MW'; 'Highest efficiency, up to 97% with energy store connected'; 'Battery or flywheel-backed versions' — batteries manage 'complete utility failure up to 30 minutes'; '99% input/output harmonic isolation'; 'Virtual unity input power factor'; rides 'voltage sags to 50% of nominal' and 'brownouts to 30% without even using the stored energy'; 'handles 100% non-linear loads as well as 100% step loads'; 'Life expectancy… easily exceeds 20 years'. The motor-generator and coupling choke act 'as a rotating isolation transformer', 'power capacitors are eliminated', and the machine is 'inherently capable of clearing short circuit faults'. UBTD+ couples the same machine to a diesel engine: '500kW up to 40MW', low and medium voltage, 'adjustable diesel start delay (seconds to minutes)', 'critical and emergency supplies can be isolated or combined'; named sizes include UBTD+ 2700 at 2,250 kW and 35 kV (American Regent, 2024) and sixteen UBTD units totalling 34.4 MVA on one IP system (a global bank, 2025). DeRUPS™ 'integrates external diesel generators with a UNIBLOCK™ UBT+ Rotary UPS through an intelligent control system' so 'Generator count need not match UPS unit quantity' and 'Loads can operate from gensets while UPS undergoes maintenance', with 'simple mechanical design without freewheel clutches'.
highlights: Installed base per company: 'more than 6000 high power UPS units' and 'over 7000 kinetic energy storage devices' (2021), technicians 'taking care of over 9000 units of high power UPS equipment in over 40 countries'; the 2008 'world's largest single Diesel UPS (3000 kVA)'

The reference installations the company leads with are institutional: 'from the Federal Reserve and the NYSE, to the Bank of England, the LSE and the CIA' (Langley brochure 2026), a classified US Government data center at Langley, Virginia (2017, repeat order Feb 2026), NYC 911 (eight EC UBT+ 675 battery modules, >5 MW), General Motors (eight MV UNIBLOCK 3000 kVA with two 21 MJ POWERBRIDGE each)

Medium-voltage direct connection is the differentiator the static majors have only recently answered: installations at 10 kV, 20 kV, 24 kV and 35 kV are company-documented; Rolls-Royce's competing dynamic UPS is likewise offered 'to 15 kV class' (Consulting-Specifying Engineer, 2024)
Odense University Hospital (handover mid-2025) is described by the company as 'Scandinavia's second largest battery-free DRUPS system'
productsAndServices.positioning: Where a buyer wants one machine per block with no battery room, medium-voltage connection and large fault current — finance, government, semiconductor, Tier IV colocation — UNIBLOCK is the incumbent; the trade against it, quantified in Schneider Electric's White Paper 222 (2016), is efficiency at part load ('one of the top DRUPS in market' peaking ~92% against static up to 97.6%), 8–12 s of flywheel ride-through against minutes of battery, single-vendor overhaul, and non-modular scaling. Langley concedes hyperscale 'moved away from Piller rotary technology' toward battery-static UPS.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct via Piller subsidiaries and distributors; rental and containerised units through Piller's hire fleet; long-term service through the Unity Service Pack.
targetSegments: Financial institutions, exchanges and government facilities
Colocation and enterprise data centers, especially IP-bus Tier IV designs
Hospitals, airports, broadcasting and continuous-process industry
productsAndServices.roadmap: No new UBT+/UBTD+ ratings announced; the platform's growth path is the UB-V generation and the Bilshausen capacity step-up.

productsAndServices.name: Isolated Parallel (IP) bus system
productsAndServices.description: Piller's trademarked ring topology, per its product page: 'combines isolated-redundant and parallel-redundant UPS configurations offering outstanding maintainability'; 'fault tolerant and concurrently maintainable'; 'Modules operate at approximately 97% efficiency'; the 'system naturally balances in all conditions and avoids unnecessary switchgear operations under fault conditions'; 'Low Voltage deployment up to 20MW' (medium voltage to 40 MW per the UBT+ brochure); 'Over 500MVA of IP Bus systems deployed globally to date'; 'Tier IV Scheme approved by Uptime Institute'. Independent account (Uptime Institute Journal, 2015): NEXTDC S1 Sydney ran 12+1 continuous-rated 1,336 kW Piller DRUPS on an IP bus (11.5 MW, later 14+1 for 13.8 MW), chosen to eliminate batteries, static switches and 'complex switching', giving N+1 'without switching' at efficiency 'approaching 98%'.
highlights: NEXTDC B2 Brisbane: 'World first – using Piller IP-Bus technology, the Uptime Institute awards Asia Pacific's first Tier IV Certification of Constructed Facility' (company); NEXTDC's S1, S2, S3, M1 and M3 pages document Piller rotary UPS with Penske and mtu engines

ABB, introducing a ring bus for static UPS in 2014, stated the topology 'has traditionally only been deployed with rotary UPS systems' because static units lacked fault-current capability and risked DC-link back-feed — the fault-current argument for rotary, made by a static vendor

A 'leading global bank' in Europe doubled its Piller IP system from eight UBTD units (17.2 MVA, since 2012) to sixteen (34.4 MVA) in 2025; Telehouse Frankfurt Building M lists '3 x DRUPS in IP-Bus system configuration' (vendor implied, not stated)
productsAndServices.positioning: The alternative to catcher (block-redundant) and distributed-redundant static schemes: redundancy in choke impedance rather than in a static transfer switch. Its home is the operator who wants Tier IV without 2N and without a battery room; the static majors answer with ring-bus variants of their own (ABB, 2014) and, at medium voltage, ABB's HiPerGuard.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Engineered as a system by Piller with the UPS order; consulting engineers (e.g. Hurley Palmer Flatt on the 2020 webinar series) specify it.
targetSegments: Tier III/IV colocation and enterprise data centers
Banks and exchanges
Any UPS block from ~5 MW to 40 MW that must be concurrently maintainable
productsAndServices.roadmap: None announced; the IPCS 10 MW module for microgrids (four UB-V units behind one 10 MW choke) is the same idea applied to generation.

productsAndServices.name: POWERBRIDGE™ kinetic energy storage (PB6+, PB21, PB60+) and battery options
productsAndServices.description: The flywheel behind UNIBLOCK, UB-V, CPM and SHIELDX. Per company pages: 'kinetic energy storage ranging from 3.6MJ up to 60MJ+ per unit'; the PB60+ is 'the World's largest, commercially available kinetic energy store, delivering from 3MJ to over 60MJ… and can even provide 1MW of ride-through power for over 60 seconds' and 'can deliver power above 3MW'; 'vertically mounted flywheel and generator utilising magnetic bearing technology'; 'Bearings are greased automatically from a reservoir'; 'The unit operates in an inert environment'; 'Life time > 20 years'; 'Floor Space Up to 90% can be saved when compared to batteries'; 'air conditioning is not required'; and 'a POWERBRIDGE™ will absorb energy at the same rate as it can deliver… can stabilize a diesel or natural gas engine'. Deployed pairs: two 21 MJ units per MV UNIBLOCK at General Motors, two PB21 per 2.5 MW UB-V in the Power of 10 module, PB60+ units giving 3,600 kW at PT Santos Jaya Abadi. Battery alternative: UPS 'designed for both conventional lead-acid batteries and lithium-ion batteries' — a 3.6 MW German data-centre UPS used LFP with UL 9540A certification for 7 minutes of bridging; the M+ Series offers Li-ion cabinets from 250 to 1,200 kW. No rotational speed is published for POWERBRIDGE.
highlights: Company positioning: 'no toxic batteries', 'stored energy levels are certain', 'no environmental disposal issue'; the UBT+ brochure claims '3 times longer bridging time from Piller POWERBRIDGE™' than earlier flywheels

Piller's history page dates '21 MWs kinetic energy storage' development to 2008–2014 and the Magnetic Bearings Technologies acquisition to 1992 — the bearing technology that lets the rotor run in an inert enclosure
The bidirectional absorb-and-inject capability is what SHIELDX productises for AI load steps
productsAndServices.positioning: Against VRLA and lithium-ion strings on the seconds-to-a-generator-start job: no battery room, no fire-code review under NFPA 855, no replacement cycle, a state of charge read from speed; against them on duration it concedes minutes. Active Power's CleanSource flywheels (6.2 and 10.2 MJ, 10,000 and 7,700 rpm) are the group's low-voltage counterpart.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Sold with the UPS or stabilizer it backs; also rented in Piller's hire fleet.
targetSegments: Every rotary UPS and SHIELDX installation
Microgrid and engine stabilization
Sites where battery rooms are unwanted (semiconductor, research, hospitals)
productsAndServices.roadmap: None announced beyond the PB60+ already in service.

productsAndServices.name: Active Power CleanSource® flywheel UPS family (PLUS SMS/MMS, XT, HD, POWERHOUSE, GenSTART)
productsAndServices.description: Austin, Texas — 'a stand-alone business within the Piller group' since November 2016, with a '135,000+ square feet' ISO 9001 plant and 'annual production capacity exceeding 300MW'. CleanSource PLUS MMS per the June 2022 datasheet: modules of 333/667/1,000/1,333 kW (370–1,480 kVA) expandable to 2,667 kW, 'Integrated Steel Flywheel spinning at 10,000RPM', flywheel run time '100% 18s, 75% 24s, 50% 35s, 25% 62s', 'Flywheel Recharge Time < 3 min (nominal) at 65kW', 'Efficiency – Energy Storage Online 98%', 'Transient +/-1% within 50 mSec for 100% load step', UL 1778 listed; SMS single modules 333 kW (480 V) / 300 kW (CE) with '6.2 MJ' and 'Up to 2 minutes' load-dependent. CleanSource HD: '750kVA/675kW', 'STORES 10.2 MJ OF ENERGY', '7,700RPM', run time 15 s at 100% load to 56 s at 25%, 'Up to 7 UPS systems can be paralleled… supporting over 4.725MW', 'UPS Efficiency 96.5% @ 50% load up to 98% @ 100% load', 65 kA withstand, two cabinets on '35 square feet'. CleanSource XT: 225–250 kW modules to 2,000 kW. POWERHOUSE: '1,333kW OF MODULAR UPS IN A STANDARD ISO CONTAINER', customisable '333kW up to 2,667kW', −25 °C to 50 °C, 'just 4.4kW to spin all four wheels', '97%' at 50% load, TCO claimed '32% less on day one and 36% lower over a 20 year lifespan' versus static UPS with lithium. GenSTART supplies '1725 Cold Cranking Amps' from the UPS output to a generator starter, replacing starter batteries.
highlights: Nebius Group, Mäntsälä, Finland: 'Over 200 CleanSource® UPS units' for a 75 MW expansion (June 2025), built in Austin with Piller Germany; per Langley's 2025 report 'the same customer placed a much larger order for an AI data centre in the USA for delivery this year' and Active Power's 2026 output is 'increasing four-fold on 2025' — the group's largest AI-hall reference and the one that lands in the corpus's neocloud set

Named users per Active Power: Tesla (two CleanSource PLUS MMS at 2.4 MW each plus a 333 kW SMS, 'eight additional 4.8MW installations planned'), Mayo Clinic, Parkland Hospital, Stratasys, Albuquerque Airport; Langley: Active Power was 'around 10% of Piller Group revenues and profits' in 2023 and 2024

Independent context: Active Power's FY2015 10-K showed $57.4M revenue and a $6.5M net loss; the 2016 sale to Langley's Piller USA was 'for a nominal purchase price, plus the assumption of all debt, liabilities' and framed by its CEO as preferable to 'a costly liquidation process'; Caterpillar had distributed its flywheels as the 'Cat UPS' from 2000 (renewed 2008)
OSHPD/HCAI seismic pre-approval OSP-0829 (July 2025) for hospitals; 400 kW rooftop solar on the Austin plant (Jan 2025)
productsAndServices.positioning: The low-voltage, modular flywheel answer to modular static UPS: 'clear alternative to modular static UPS systems reliant on battery storage', 'battery failures are the leading cause of UPS load loss' (company claims). It concedes minutes of autonomy to batteries and competes on footprint, no battery replacement, and TCO claims; flywheel-only rivals are VYCON/Calnetix, Amber Kinetics and Beacon Power, static rivals the top-five UPS majors.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: US customers direct from Austin; international customers 'through Piller's global network of sales and service subsidiaries'; Piller lists 'CleanSource® – Static UPS with Flywheel, 250 – 1200kW' in its own product menu.
targetSegments: AI and enterprise data centers (Nebius, Tesla)
Healthcare (Mayo, Parkland — seismic pre-approval)
Industrial, transportation, defense, broadcasting
productsAndServices.roadmap: Production 'four-fold on 2025' in 2026 (Langley interim); a 'much larger' US AI data-centre order from the Finland customer for 2026 delivery; no new model announced.

productsAndServices.name: Critical Power Module (CPM) with flywheel — 225 kW to 2.4 MW
productsAndServices.description: Skid-mounted flywheel UPS built on POWERBRIDGE PB6+ storage. Per company pages and the 2016 datasheet: '225kW to 2.4MW (300/360kW modules scalable to 2400/2880kW)'; 'Efficiency above 96% at 25% load (IEC 62040-3)', efficiency that can 'approach 99% at full load' ('up to 99%* (*480V 60Hz without DC store)'), 'higher than 98%' in VFD mode; '100kA short circuit withstand'; 'Ambient up to 50°C for optimum use of free cooling'; 'Extended (10 year) major maintenance interval' — 'No substantial work is necessary within the first 10 years of service'; 'Unity input power factor (>0.99)'; 'Parallel capability up to 8 units'; five operating modes 'Mode 1 (VFI), Mode 2 (VI), Mode 3 (VFI2), Mode 4 (VFD), Mode 5 (ERM)' including an Enhanced Redundancy Mode; '380V-480V', '50 & 60Hz'; footprint '2450w x 900d x 1900h' mm per 300/360 kW module, 'up to 75% of the space normally taken up can be saved'.
highlights: The product that brings IEC 62040-3 mode selection to a flywheel unit — the same VFI/VI/VFD dial static vendors sell, on kinetic storage
Company positioning: 'No Battery risk, no Battery replacement'; 'Ideal for rapid deployment' with PDUs on the skid
productsAndServices.positioning: Sits between the CleanSource modules and the multi-megawatt UNIBLOCK machines: a containerable, low-voltage block for the 0.2–2.4 MW range where static modular UPS (Schneider Galaxy, Vertiv, Eaton) is the default.
targetSegments: Data centers and edge deployments
Manufacturing, healthcare, banking, communications, aviation, naval

productsAndServices.name: Static UPS and static transfer switches — M+ Series (M+500, M+1200), APOSTAR, APOTRANS
productsAndServices.description: The re-entry into the segment hyperscale took to battery-static UPS. M+500 launched 12–17 June 2024 at Data Centre World Frankfurt; M+1200 followed. Per company pages: '10 x 50 kW power modules delivering 500 kW of UPS per unit', 'Infinitely scalable', 'hot-swappable modular design', '250kW to 1200kW' per unit, efficiency 'up to 97%', 'wide input voltage and frequency tolerance', 'High short circuit capacity duration', with 'Lithium-ion Backup Battery' cabinets in a 'modular parallel design' with 'automatic module failure detection and exit', and three service tiers. Langley's account of why it exists (AR 2023): hyperscale 'has moved away from Piller's tailored solutions to a more commoditised cookie cutter approach… discussions were held with a major Chinese manufacturer of these volume produced hardware with a view to re-entering the segment. Piller's profound expertise… paired with cost-effective hardware'; AR 2024: 'The hyperscalers have moved away from Piller rotary technology in recent years in favour of battery-static UPS technology but after more than three years of development, Piller announced its return to the sector with its M+ battery-static UPS offering'. The product page names no OEM partner. APOSTAR static UPS covers 3–500 kVA ('true online UPS with VFI SS 1111 characteristic double voltage conversion'); APOTRANS is a thyristor static transfer switch from 25 to 1,600 A whose 'changeover occurs within milliseconds', 'available as standalone units or chassis based for integration directly into switchgear' for 'isolated redundancy or distributed redundancy'.
highlights: Dr Zaki Slgini at launch: 'Our customers told us they wanted rapidly deployable hot-swappable high-density modular static UPS. With the M+500 Piller has responded'
'Available through Piller subsidiaries and partners in approximately 40 countries'; regional launch tour Sydney, Singapore, UK (Sep–Oct 2024)
No M+ Series order, customer or shipped volume has been published by the company or found in independent press as of September 2026
productsAndServices.positioning: Head-on with Schneider Electric Galaxy VXL (500–1,250 kW frames, 125 kW modules), Vertiv Trinergy (1.5–2.5 MW blocks to 20 MW) and Eaton 9395X (to 1,700 kVA) — a late entrant at 500–1,200 kW per unit whose stated edge is Piller's service network and short-circuit capacity, and whose hardware provenance the company has not disclosed.
targetSegments: Core and edge data centers
High-density rack environments
productsAndServices.roadmap: The company said in October 2024 it would 'release the next iteration of the M+ Series in early 2025' — the M+1200 is now listed; nothing further announced.

productsAndServices.name: Frequency converters, aircraft ground power, naval and shore power, and the Grid series
productsAndServices.description: The non-data-centre half of the catalogue. 50/60 Hz converters: static 'From 30kVA up to 500kVA', rotary motor-generator sets '125kVA to 2300kVA' with 'Up to 12% automatic line drop compensation'. 400 Hz aviation: 'Static APOJET AJS: 5kVA to 200kVA' solid-state converters with IGBT rectifiers ('THD at input current < 5%'), 'Rotary APOJET AJR: 20 to 150kVA', 'APOJET AJT Gatebox: 90-180kVA', APOCOIL cable coiling and 28 V DC ground power units at 400 and 600 A ('Peak current up to 2000A'); centralised ground power at King Abdulaziz International Airport, Jeddah 'at stands up to 450m from the converter room'. Naval and shore power: 'Frequency converters up to 1500kVA', 'Parallel operation up to 8 systems', 'Maximum reliability (MTBF 1.000.000 hours)', for 'submarines and surface ships' — Piller has built brushless submarine generators since 1975. Grid series: 'GridPB can provide significant additional inertia for island grids utilising large amounts of variable renewable energy'; 'GridGate' for 'Datacentre microgrid solutions… stabilising voltage and frequency, absorbing power variations'; the company states its flywheel systems 'are capable of additional microgrid services such as grid-forming, inertia and SCR enhancement' (synchronous condenser replacement). A semiconductor-fab reference runs 'nine 3.9 MW generator sets' exchanging 'up to a level of 5 MW in each direction' with the utility. No datasheet with MW, MVAr or inertia figures is published for the Grid series.
highlights: Langley 2025: 'Strong demand from governmental, defence, pharmaceuticals and chip manufacturing sectors were the main drivers' of Piller's record year — defence and aviation are a material part of the base that data centres are layered on
Exhibited at EURONAVAL Paris (Nov 2024) and Middle East Energy Dubai (Apr 2025, GridGate and UNIBLOCK stabilisers; ALMA Observatory Chile reference)

No independent report of a Piller grid-inertia or synchronous-condenser project with a transmission operator was found — the flywheel-syncon projects in the public record (ElectraNet Robertstown, Moneypoint) are Siemens Energy's
productsAndServices.positioning: In aviation ground power and naval converters Piller competes in a specialist field outside this corpus; the Grid series positions the same rotary machines against BESS and synchronous condensers for inertia and grid-forming on islands and campuses — a claim the SHIELDX orders are the first to monetise at scale.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct, with defence and airport procurement channels; rental fleet for aircraft GPUs and converters.
targetSegments: Civil and military airports
Navies and shipyards (shore-to-ship, on-board)

productsAndServices.name: Service, lifecycle and rental

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess that Piller's relevance to the AI buildout runs through Langley's behind-the-meter engine plant, not through the hyperscale UPS room it lost. Basis: Langley states in its own reports that hyperscale 'moved away from Piller rotary technology in recent years in favour of battery-static UPS'; that 'Every BTM solution being sold incorporates SHIELDX™'; and that more than 3 GW of such plants were signed in the year to June 2026 (Crusoe ~750 MW, Liberty 500 MW+, E-Finity 400 MW), each counterparty naming Piller. SHIELDX therefore sells one unit per 12 MW Bergen gen-set on Bergen's order book, and its volume is a function of engine sales rather than of UPS bids.

(High confidence) We assess that factory capacity, not demand, is the binding constraint on Piller through 2027. Basis: Co-CEO Seidel's 'the AI boom brings us to our capacity limits' (NW-IHK, Feb 2026; charakter.me, Apr 2026); the €20M Bilshausen programme lifts output from about 100 to about 400 large systems a year only by end-2027 (StadtRadio, May 2026); Langley's H1 2026 statement that capacity is 'sold out for this year and next, with build slots now being released for 2028' and that 'it will be 2028 before the ramp-up is complete'; Bergen's 12.5 MW engines sold out until Q2 2028. Langley already recorded in 2023 that 'capacity constraints meant that not all projects originally planned could be fulfilled within the year'. Expect 2026 growth near the ~30% Seidel guided rather than the order-intake rate.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that the rotary and flywheel franchise wins where a buyer values fault current, harmonic isolation, medium-voltage connection, no battery room and one accountable vendor per block — finance, government, semiconductor, hospitals, Tier IV colocation — and loses where the buyer standardizes on modular low-voltage blocks bought in minutes of battery autonomy from several vendors. Basis: Piller's own reference list (Federal Reserve, NYSE, Bank of England, CIA, a classified US facility, NEXTDC's Tier IV IP-bus sites, GM, a 24 kV US fab); Uptime Institute's account of NEXTDC choosing DRUPS on an IP bus to remove batteries and static switches; ABB's 2014 concession that the ring bus was rotary-only for fault-current reasons; against it, Schneider's White Paper 222 on part-load efficiency, single-vendor overhaul and scaling, and Langley's own account of hyperscale's departure. The M+ Series is the hedge back into static; no M+ order has been published in two years, so the hedge is unproven.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that SHIELDX's competitive contest is with battery buffers, not with static UPS, and that the two are being bought together rather than instead of each other. Basis: Piller positions SHIELDX against BESS ('Avoids C-rate limits, thermal stress, and degradation cycles') and claims real inertia, fault current and zero storage degradation; SemiAnalysis independently frames flywheels (5–30 s of real power) against Tesla Megapacks, which xAI uses; Crusoe's dossier shows the same campuses taking 5 GW of ON.energy medium-voltage BESS alongside the Bergen/SHIELD-X plant. The flywheel holds the seconds and the inertia; the battery holds the duration. A campus choosing only one would be the signal that this judgment is wrong.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that Piller's US tariff exposure is structural and unquantified, and that the Austin flywheel plant is its only stated US manufacturing base. Basis: UNIBLOCK, UB-V and SHIELDX are built in Germany and shipped to US projects; EU machinery has paid a 15% all-inclusive US tariff since 1 July 2026 and Section 232 derivative duties apply to many chapter 84/85 articles (Bundesregierung; Perkins Coie); no Langley or Piller statement on tariff cost, HTS treatment or US assembly of SHIELDX was found in English or German press; Active Power's 135,000 sq ft Austin plant (300 MW a year) and the 24,000 sq ft Middletown, NY facility are the US footprint on record.

(Low confidence) We assess that the execution risk to the SHIELDX book sits in the plants it is sold into rather than in Piller's product. Basis: the first 400 MW order's site — identified as Vineland, NJ only by third parties — is reported by WHYY (Aug 2026) to have had its gas-engine plan replaced by Bloom Energy fuel cells and its running generators found unpermitted by NJDEP, against Powertrain International's January schedule of all 36 engines and SHIELDX modules on site by end-2026; no source states the effect on Piller's scope. Langley's willingness to discontinue Manroland Sheetfed (744 jobs, June 2026) and its FY2026 PBT forecast cut from €282.4M to €237.8M show a parent that reprices quickly. Collection gap: Piller Group GmbH's own revenue, profit and order book are disclosed only qualitatively by Langley and once, for 2025, by the Northeim chamber of commerce; no SHIELDX or POWERBRIDGE datasheet with per-module MW, MJ or rpm exists; no independent market-share figure for Piller or the rotary niche was found; Bundesanzeiger filings sit behind paywalls; there is no analyst consensus at any level.

INDICATORS TO WATCH — *Autumn 2026, Osterode:* the 12.5 MW Bergen engine plus SHIELD-X live demonstration; a published per-module rating or datasheet would close the largest specification gap. *Q4 2026–Q1 2027:* whether the 400 MW E-Finity plant energizes on schedule with SHIELDX, or the Vineland fuel-cell switch and NJDEP compliance determination alter its scope — the first test of plant-level execution risk. *Early February 2027, Langley Annual Report 2026:* Piller's 2026 growth against the ~30% guide and the Power Solutions division against its €1,346M forecast; whether the FY2026 PBT lands near the €237.8M August guide; any Piller-level disclosure of SHIELDX units shipped. *Through 2027:* first SHIELD-X deliveries to Crusoe sites and Liberty's H2 2027 engines; a first named hyperscaler order for SHIELDX or the M+ Series would refute the hall-side judgment; a campus choosing SHIELDX without a BESS, or a BESS without SHIELDX, would sharpen the complement-versus-substitute judgment. *End-2027:* Bilshausen at ~400 large systems a year — the date after which capacity stops explaining the growth rate. *Any date:* a US assembly announcement for SHIELDX or UNIBLOCK, which would answer the tariff judgment.

relationships.context:
Bergen Engines, Piller's sister company under Langley Holdings, signed a 438 MW firm contract plus a 310 MW letter of intent with Crusoe on 3 June 2026 for 27 B36:45V20AG2 (12.5 MWe) and 20 B36:45L9AG (5 MWe) gen-sets, phased through 2027. Piller announced on 16 June 2025 that Nebius Group NV's Mäntsälä data center would receive 'Over 200 CleanSource® UPS units' for a 75 MW expansion, built at Active Power's Austin plant in collaboration with Piller Germany, with 'several hundred' units delivered during 2025. Separately, third parties (Sierra Club NJ, SJ Climate News) identify DataOne's Vineland, New Jersey campus — built for Nebius under its Microsoft contract — as the site of the 400 MW Bergen/SHIELDX plant that Langley announced without naming a location; Langley itself has never confirmed that linkage, and WHYY reported in August 2026 that the site's gas-engine plan was being replaced by Bloom Energy fuel cells.

The relationship is dual: Tesla buys Piller-group flywheel UPS for its own facilities, while Tesla Energy argues — per SemiAnalysis (Dec 2025) — that hundreds of megawatts of Megapacks are the right fix for AI load swings, the job SHIELDX is sold for, and xAI uses Megapacks for it.

relationships.note: Caterpillar distributed Active Power's flywheel UPS as the 'Cat UPS' from August 2000, renewing the agreement in 2008; the channel predates Piller's ownership and its current status is not stated by either company.
relationships.context: Data Center Knowledge reported in April 2008 that Caterpillar and Active Power had renewed a distribution agreement under which Caterpillar had sold Active Power's flywheel-based UPS as the 'Cat UPS' since August 2000, for a further three years. No source records the termination date or any current arrangement, and Active Power's post-2016 literature does not mention Caterpillar. Today the two groups meet as rival prime-mover suppliers to AI campuses: Caterpillar's diesel and gas gen-sets and Solar turbines against Bergen Engines' medium-speed gas engines, with which SHIELDX is bundled.

relationships.note: At the Vineland, NJ campus third parties identify as the first 400 MW Bergen/SHIELDX plant, WHYY reports the gas-engine plan was scrapped over emissions opposition in favour of Bloom Energy fuel cells (300 MW proposed) — a fuel-cell displacement of the engine-plus-flywheel bundle.
relationships.context: WHYY reported on 6 August 2026 that at a six-hour Vineland Planning Board hearing DataOne proposed Bloom Energy fuel cells for Phase 2 and described the earlier plan of 32 gas engines (5 for backup) plus 6 diesel gen-sets as scrapped because of public opposition over air emissions; on 28 August 2026 WHYY reported NJDEP finding no permit and no application for the generators already running on site. Neither WHYY piece names Bergen, E-Finity or Piller; the linkage of the site to the 400 MW Bergen/SHIELDX contract comes from Sierra Club NJ and SJ Climate News. What this means for Piller's SHIELDX scope on that project is not stated by any source — recorded here as the one documented case of a fuel-cell plant displacing the engine plant SHIELDX is sold with.

relationships.note: Vertiv's Trinergy static UPS (1.5–2.5 MW blocks to 20 MW) is the incumbent form Piller's UB-V rotary UPS and M+ Series static UPS compete against in AI halls; Langley concedes hyperscale 'moved away from Piller rotary technology… in favour of battery-static UPS'.
relationships.context: Vertiv sits in the top-five data-center UPS group (with Schneider Electric, Eaton, Huawei and ABB, roughly 40–42% share per MarketsandMarkets, an aggregator) that took the hyperscale UPS segment as it standardized on low-voltage modular battery-static units. Piller's answer is two-sided: the UB-V rotary machine pitched as 'a real alternative to increasingly sprawling multiple static UPS solutions', and the M+ Series launched in June 2024 to compete on static's own terms. Vertiv's dossier records Trinergy as the large-UPS franchise the 800 VDC architecture threatens; Piller has published no 800 VDC position.

relationships.note: Schneider Electric's Galaxy VXL (500–1,250 kW frames, to 5 MW) competes with the M+ Series and UB-V; Schneider's White Paper 222 is the quantified static-side case against DRUPS that Piller's positioning answers.
relationships.context: Schneider Electric's 2016 White Paper 222, 'Diesel Rotary UPS (DRUPS) vs. Static UPS: A Quantitative Comparison', found a top DRUPS peaking near 92% efficiency against static up to 97.6%, 68% lower energy losses for static at 43–47% utilisation, 8–12 s of flywheel ride-through against 5–6 min of battery, single-vendor DRUPS overhaul, and a 7.2% ten-year TCO advantage for static in a 2N IT-plus-cooling case — while conceding DRUPS a 10.6% advantage when the rental value of its smaller footprint is credited in an IT-only design. Piller's UB-V literature is written against this framing ('up to 98% at 100% load and 97% at 50% load… compared with static UPS which typically operate around 96.3%'). Schneider is also a named NVIDIA 800 VDC partner; Piller is not.

relationships.note: Eaton's 9395X large static UPS and its static transfer switches compete with Piller's UB-V/UNIBLOCK and APOTRANS lines; Eaton's guide in this app is the corpus's other UPS teaching source.
relationships.context: Eaton is one of the top-five data-center UPS vendors (MarketsandMarkets, aggregator) whose battery-static architecture displaced rotary UPS at hyperscale, per Langley's own account. The two companies' teaching in this app is complementary: Eaton's dossier and guide carry the double-conversion-versus-eco-mode dial and the outage choreography; Piller's carry the rotary machine, the flywheel and the isolated-parallel bus. Eaton's supercapacitor fast-cycle modules for 800 VDC racks are a millisecond-scale store adjacent to — but not a substitute for — the second-scale flywheel.

relationships.note: ABB's HiPerGuard medium-voltage static UPS (2.5 MW units, 25 MW parallel, to 34.5 kV) attacks the medium-voltage niche rotary UPS held; ABB's 2014 ring-bus release conceded that the ring topology 'has traditionally only been deployed with rotary UPS systems' for fault-current reasons.
relationships.context: ABB introduced a ring-bus (isolated-parallel-style) architecture for static UPS in 2014, stating the topology had been rotary-only because static units lacked fault-current capability and risked DC-link back-feed — an independent statement of the rotary machine's protection advantage from a static vendor. ABB's HiPerGuard, deployed at Applied Digital's Polaris Forge campuses in 25 MW blocks, is the static industry's move onto the medium-voltage ground where Piller's UNIBLOCK and UB-V have sold at 10–35 kV. ABB's guide also carries the corpus's one paragraph on flywheels as grid stabilizers.

policyExposure.regime: US import tariffs on German-built equipment (Section 232 derivatives; EU–US 15% ceiling)
policyExposure.exposure: Piller's UNIBLOCK, UB-V and SHIELDX systems are manufactured at Osterode and Bilshausen, Germany and shipped to US behind-the-meter projects; Active Power's flywheel UPS are built in Austin, Texas. Since 1 July 2026 EU goods including HTS chapter 84 machinery pay a flat 15% all-inclusive US tariff under the EU–US framework (Bundesregierung FAQ); the restructured Section 232 metals regime assesses 50% on covered steel and aluminium articles and listed derivatives — many in chapters 84/85 — on full customs value from 6 April 2026, with 'metal-intensive industrial base and electrical grid equipment' capped at 15% including MFN to end-2027 and EU/UK/Japan/Korea keeping agreement rates (Perkins Coie, Global Trade & Sanctions Law). The IEEPA tariffs were ruled unlawful on 20 February 2026 and a Section 122 surcharge ran 24 February–24 July 2026 (Bruegel). No source states Piller's specific HTS treatment, tariff cost or any US assembly of UNIBLOCK or SHIELDX.

policyExposure.regime: US stationary engine and data-center generator rules (RICE NESHAP/NSPS; state and local air permits)
policyExposure.exposure: The diesel engines in Piller's UBTD+ diesel rotary UPS are stationary emergency engines under US rules — unlimited emergency hours, 100 hours a year of non-emergency running and 50 hours of demand response — and EPA's 1 May 2025 clarification on data-center backup generators said it is 'evaluating more substantive changes' while states tighten generator rules (Sidley, Encino Environmental). The larger exposure is indirect: SHIELDX is sold into islanded gas-engine plants that need local air permits, and at the Vineland, NJ campus third parties tie to the first 400 MW Bergen/SHIELDX order, NJDEP found in August 2026 that generators were operating with no permit and no application while the developer moved its plan to fuel cells (WHYY).

policyExposure.regime: EU Medium Combustion Plant Directive and UK Specified Generator controls (DRUPS engines in Europe)
policyExposure.exposure: Directive (EU) 2015/2193 covers permanently installed combustion plant of 1–50 MW thermal input — which techUK notes captures 'virtually every' data-centre engine, including the diesels in DRUPS — with member-state discretion to exempt emergency plant running under 500 hours a year; the UK's Specified Generator rules add conditions on demand-side response and testing hours, and EU Stage V applies to transportable sets such as Piller's containerised hire units (techUK; Axces). Sources address the engine class generally, not Piller by name.
